Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source mug has been relocated to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: Pass when visual correspondence and spatial evidence support that the source mug has been relocated to the right of the headphones in the edited image. Evaluate correspondence using the combined evidence of body proportions, rim, handle geometry, scale, appearance, and placement; exact color or appearance preservation is not required. A mug on the right alone does not establish the requested relocation. Fail when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise has not reached the requested right-side position, including identifiable movement that stops short of that position. Use unknown when competing correspondences remain unresolved and would change whether the condition is satisfied. Neither failure to prove completion nor a blurred remnant alone establishes failure.
node.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare that mug with both edited mugs—the pale mug left of the headphones and the mug right of them—and inspect the blue blurred patch at far left as possible residual evidence. Assess the candidates without assigning identity from color alone or requiring an unchanged handle orientation. Account for the different image framing, scale, and headphone arrangement by comparing object-relative positions rather than raw pixel coordinates. Determine whether the combined evidence establishes relocation of the source mug to the right of the edited headphones; leave the result unknown if the available evidence cannot resolve that condition.

node_traces.evidence: The source light-blue mug is left of the headphones. In the edited image, the mug on the right of the headphones has a similar tapered body and rim proportions and comparable scale, supporting it as the source mug despite its different appearance and handle orientation. A separate pale mug remains left of the headphones, while the blue blurred patch at far left is consistent with residual evidence rather than the mug itself. The corresponding mug is therefore established to be right of the edited headphones.

Tighten the decision to weigh the full set of identity cues and whether the source mug itself reached the right side, explicitly resolving competing candidates and residual evidence before passing; use unknown if that evidence remains unresolved. Do not infer failure merely from the blur or force a label from the aggregate reference.
